title: ～ても — “even if ～”
summary: Shows that the result does not change even if the condition holds. Verbs: te-form + も; i-adjectives: ～くても; nouns and na-adjectives: ～でも.

body.p: 雨が降っても、試合はします means that the game goes ahead despite rain. It pairs well with intensifiers: いくら考えても, どんなに～ても.
ても is for conditions that have not happened yet (or general ones). For surprise or complaint about a fact that has already happened, use のに.

examples.ja: 雨（あめ）が降（ふ）っても、試合（しあい）はします。
examples.romaji: Ame ga futte mo, shiai wa shimasu.
examples.tr: Even if it rains, we'll have the game.

examples.ja: いくら考（かんが）えても、答（こた）えが分（わ）からない。
examples.romaji: Ikura kangaete mo, kotae ga wakaranai.
examples.tr: No matter how much I think, I can't figure out the answer.

examples.ja: 少（すこ）し高（たか）くても、体（からだ）にいい物（もの）を買（か）いたい。
examples.romaji: Sukoshi takakute mo, karada ni ii mono o kaitai.
examples.tr: Even if it's a little expensive, I want to buy things that are good for my body.

pitfalls: I-adjectives are 高くても, not 高いても.
For complaint about an already-happened fact, use のに.
